data.title: Altria Could Expand Next-Generation Products With Imperial Deal — Market Talk
data.description: An Altria buyout of smaller London-listed peer Imperial Brands would be logical and highly likely to proceed, Citi's Simon Hales and Sunny Wadhwani write. The Marlboro cigarette maker said it was considering an all-cash bid for the company behind the Davidoff and Gauloises. Because Altria only operates in the U.S. with a limited exposure to next-generation products, buying Imperial Brands would diversify its traditional cigarette business while expanding its lineup of heated tobacco, vapes, and oral nicotine produts, the analysts say. Citi has a neutral rating on Altria's stock and a $72 target price. Shares are down 2.5% at $74.39 in premarket trading. (ian.walker@wsj.com)

data.title: HubSpot downgraded by Argus amid worries about turnaround
data.description:
Key points:
  • HubSpot was downgraded by investment firm Argus on Friday amid worries about the marketing software company's turnaround.
  • Shares rose fractionally in premarket trading.
  • “We see HubSpot as a company in turnaround. HubSpot's management has been swept away, and cofounder Brian Halligan has returned to the CEO role,” Argus analyst Joseph Bonner wrote in a note to clients. “But can HubSpot find its place in the emerging agentic AI paradigm? HubSpot is an early-stage customer relationship management software company focused on small and midsize businesses that have traditionally been overlooked by larger CRM providers. The price sensitivity and increasing reluctance of customers to close new deals is impacting HubSpot. HUBS touts its broad platform of services as an advantage in a market where customers are looking to consolidate spending at a smaller number of vendors. Like many peers, it has restructured several times, laying off staff and consolidating real estate leases, which has supported margins. However, we may have to wait until 4Q results for new management to reveal its turnaround plans.”
  • Bonner lowered his rating on HubSpot to Hold from Buy and removed his price target.

data.title: Kazakh banks raise $1.5 billion to fund private takeover of gold miner Altynalmas
data.description:
A banking syndicate led by Kazakhstan's largest bank, Halyk , has raised $1.5 billion to fund private investor Central Asia Resources Holding Ltd's acquisition of Kazakh gold miner Altynalmas (ALMS.KZ), Halyk said on Friday.

Central Asia Resources Holding Ltd signed an agreement in March to acquire 100% of Altynalmas, currently majority owned by Dutch company Gouden Reserves B.V., a filing by the buyer to the Astana International Exchange showed.

Central Asia Resources issued $1.53 billion in unsecured bonds earlier this week to help finance its acquisition of Altynalmas, one of Kazakhstan's largest gold miners, it said in a separate exchange filing.

Kazakh entrepreneur Shakhmurat Mutalip, who owns a 39.3% stake in mining company Eurasian Resources Group, is one of the shareholders in Central Asian Resources.

The banking syndicate comprises five Kazakh banks: Halyk Bank, Eurasian Bank, Alatau City Bank, Bank CentreCredit and Bank RBK, according to London-listed Halyk's statement. Financing is provided "on market terms with collateral covering the full amount of the financing”, it added.

The closing date for the transaction has not been announced.

data.title: Brazil's primary surplus tops expectations in October
data.description:
Brazil's central government recorded a primary surplus of 52.3 billion reais ($9.25 billion) in October, Treasury data showed on Friday, above the 47.6 billion reais surplus forecast by economists polled by Reuters.

In the 12 months through October, Latin America's largest economy posted a primary deficit of 35.6 billion reais, equivalent to 0.27% of its gross domestic product (GDP).

  • The strong monthly result was driven by a 5.6% real increase in net revenue, amid record tax collection and a sharp rise in oil royalty and crude sales revenue as oil prices climbed

  • Total expenditure fell 0.2% in real terms from a year earlier, mainly reflecting lower healthcare spending, the Treasury said

  • Government officials said earlier this week they expect to end the year with an effective primary deficit of around 0.5% of GDP

  • The formal 2026 target calls for a primary surplus of 0.25% of GDP for the central government

  • However, Brazil's fiscal framework allows certain expenditures to be excluded from the target calculation and includes a tolerance band of 0.25 percentage point in either direction

data.title: Canada Posts 3Q Current-Account Surplus of C$4.48 Billion — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada posted a third-quarter current-account surplus, marking the first time in about four years the country has recorded two consecutive quarterly surpluses, though it was smaller than expected.

Canada's current account, the broadest indicator of its trading and investing relationship with other nations, posted a seasonally adjusted surplus of 4.48 billion Canadian dollars ($3.14 billion) in the third quarter, Statistics Canada said Friday. That fell short of expectations for a C$9.4 billion surplus, according to Bank of Nova Scotia.

The data agency revised the previous quarter's surplus to C$6.10 billion, from an earlier estimate of C$8.84 billion.

Statistics Canada said the third-quarter surplus from merchandise-goods trade was largely unchanged from the previous quarter. Exports rose 0.2% nonannualized in the July-to-September period to C$232 billion, with gains in nine of the 13 sectors tracked. Exports of energy products declined in the third quarter, but from a record high in the previous three-month period as Canada benefits from higher crude-oil prices. Imports rose 0.3% to C$221.6 billion, led by electrical equipment and industrial machinery.

The current-account report also indicated that foreign-direct investment into Canada rose nearly 13% in the third quarter to C$33.61 billion, driven by foreign-led dealmaking. More than half of the foreign-direct investment was focused on the energy and mining sector, Statistics Canada said.

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: Robusta coffee heads further away from 3-year low; cocoa, sugar also gain
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE headed further away from this week's 3-year lows on Friday amid lacklustre farmer selling in top grower Vietnam, while cocoa and sugar also gained, setting fresh one-month peaks.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee rose 3.7% to $2,936 a metric ton at 1347 GMT, after setting a 3-year low of $2,709 on Wednesday.

* "Farmers are increasingly reluctant to sell," said a dealer based in Vietnam.

* He explained that if prices don't recover, he expects farmers to sell at most 35% of their crop before the Tet holiday in February, as they are banking on this year's dry weather and next year's El Nino peak to tighten supplies.

* Arabica coffee rose 4.2% to $2.7120 per lb, after hitting a five-month low on Wednesday.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar (SBH7) rose 2.9% to 18.87 cents per lb, having hit a fresh one-month high of 19.10 cents earlier.

* France's main sugar groups Tereos and Cristal Union have offered financial support to beet growers hit by drought and heatwaves, seeking to maintain plantings for the 2027 crop as Europe faces a sugar shortfall.

* The real currency in top sugar grower Brazil rallied as markets cheered news that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva had picked a market-friendly bank executive to be his next finance chief.

* A strong real deters selling of dollar-based commodities like sugar by lowering returns in local currency terms.

* The global sugar deficit in the 2026/27 season will be slightly larger than previously expected, with a weaker outlook for production in India, Green Pool forecast.

* White sugar rose 1% to $527.50 a ton, having hit a fresh one-month high of $534.40 earlier.

COCOA

* London cocoa rose 2.3% to £4,316 per ton, having hit its highest since late October at £4,335.

* The supply outlook continues to worsen in top growers Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador, though there is ample availability of cocoa for now from the bumper 2025/26 crop.

* New York cocoa rose 2% to $5,545 a ton, having hit its highest since early November at $5,575.

($1 = 25,847.0000 dong)
